[page[title]]

WebApplicationExtensions must consume the service provider to start application services.

What The Standard says

“system operations” — Configuration models handle startup concerns and underlying system operations. Application startup extensions therefore belong at this boundary rather than inside business services. read it here.
“service provider” — The Standard's encapsulated composition example builds a service provider and resolves the clients that must be initialized. WebApplicationExtensions applies the same pattern to starting application services. read it here.

Why it matters

Application startup should resolve work through the configured service provider so hosted and background services use the same lifetimes and dependencies as the rest of the app. Constructing them directly would bypass composition and make startup a second dependency system.

Bad code example

// Violates STXAPP004: WebApplicationExtensions must consume the service provider to start application services.
public static WebApplication StartSchoolServices(
    this WebApplication application) =>
        application;

Good code example

// Follows STXAPP004
public static WebApplication StartSchoolServices(
    this WebApplication application)
{
    application.Services
        .GetRequiredService<ISchoolBackgroundService>()
        .Start();

    return application;
}
